projects.name: Lone Star Solar I
projects.narrative: Lone Star Solar I is a 500 MW single-axis-tracker PV plant in Pecos County, Texas, anchored by a 15-year corporate PPA with Meta. The project relies on Tier-1 Chinese and Southeast-Asian module supply, leaving it materially exposed to Section 301 escalation and UFLPA-driven CBP detentions, while its returns hinge on the durability of the §48E ITC and ERCOT interconnection timing.

projects.name: Vineyard Wind Phase II
projects.offtake_status: OREC contracts with Massachusetts (3-state RFP), price under review
policy_dependencies: Merchant Marine Act of 1920 (Jones Act) — installation vessels
EO on offshore-wind leasing — review and pause
projects.narrative: Vineyard Wind Phase II is an 800 MW fixed-bottom offshore wind project on the BOEM OCS-A 0501 lease. Capital-intensity is dominated by Siemens Gamesa 14 MW turbines and POSCO-supplied monopile steel, both of which sit in trade-action crosshairs. The schedule is at the mercy of BOEM permitting and Jones Act vessel availability, and the project's IRR hinges on the OREC re-pricing and the §45Y PTC remaining intact through 2028.

projects.name: Mojave Battery Storage Hub
projects.narrative: Mojave Battery Storage Hub is a 250 MW / 1 GWh standalone LFP BESS contracted for resource-adequacy in CAISO. With Chinese-cell content above 80%, the project's economics are squarely exposed to Section 301 escalation on HTS 8507.60 (current 25% → proposed 25-50%), and its tax equity hinges on §48E remaining technology-neutral and §45X manufacturing credits flowing to its domestic cell partner.

projects.name: Permian Hydrogen Hub
projects.offtake_status: Letter of intent with ExxonMobil for ammonia feedstock; no firm offtake
policy_dependencies: IRC §45V production tax credit (Treasury three-pillars rule)
DOE H2Hubs program funding (selected H2Hubs round 1)
projects.narrative: Permian Hydrogen Hub is a 200 MW PEM electrolyzer co-located with new utility PV and 24/7 PPAs, structured to qualify for the top $3/kg §45V tier under Treasury's three-pillars rule. With no firm offtake yet and most of the IRR tied to the §45V structure, the project is exposed to any Treasury softening of incrementality / hourly-matching requirements and to slippage in the H2Hubs milestone payments.

projects.name: I-95 EV Charging Network
projects.offtake_status: State NEVI awards across 8 states; site host revenue share
policy_dependencies: Buy America Build America (BABA) — FHWA waivers
projects.narrative: I-95 EV Charging Network is a 1,200-site DC fast-charging rollout funded through NEVI state awards across 8 states, with site economics layered on host revenue share. The project's risk profile is dominated by federal policy continuity — NEVI obligations, §30C refueling credit, and BABA domestic-content waivers — and is comparatively light on macro and trade exposure relative to the generation projects in the portfolio.

factors.title: IRA Repeal or §48E ITC Phase-Down Risk
factors.description: Republican reconciliation proposals (2025 budget bills) include full repeal or accelerated phase-out of IRC §48E technology-neutral ITC, which currently provides a 30–40% investment tax credit baseline for this project. Loss of the §48E ITC at full capex of $600M would destroy approximately $180M in tax credit value, collapsing the project's equity IRR below the 10% threshold.
factors.citation: IRC §48E (IRA §13702); House Ways & Means reconciliation discussion draft, 119th Congress; One Big Beautiful Bill Act, H.R. 1 (2025)

factors.title: Treasury §48E Domestic Content Bonus Guidance Delay
factors.description: The 10% domestic content bonus adder under §48E requires IRS/Treasury final guidance on qualifying components and cost allocation methodology; delayed or restrictive final rules (beyond proposed regs REG-100908-23) could disqualify First Solar's 20% module share from satisfying the 40% domestic content threshold, eliminating ~$18–24M in bonus credit value.
factors.citation: IRC §48E(a)(3); Treasury NPRM REG-100908-23 (68 FR 41959, Aug. 2023); IRS Notice 2023-29

factors.title: ERCOT GIS Queue Reform Interconnection Delay
factors.description: PUCT/ERCOT's ongoing Generator Interconnection Study (GIS) reform and restudies under the new study process (NPRR 1196/1197 cluster methodology) risk pushing Lone Star Solar I's Q2 2027 COD by 6–18 months, triggering PPA termination rights for Meta and forcing merchant exposure on 80% of contracted revenues.
factors.citation: PUCT Docket 54530; ERCOT NPRR 1196, NPRR 1197; FERC Order 2023 (state analogue applicability)

factors.title: AD/CVD Expansion to Malaysia and Southeast Asia Modules
factors.description: USITC/Commerce AD/CVD investigations into crystalline silicon PV cells and modules from Cambodia, Malaysia, Thailand, and Vietnam (initiated 2024, preliminary determinations expected 2025) could impose duties of 40–200%+ on JA Solar's Malaysian-origin modules representing 25% of this project's module supply, increasing capex by an estimated $24–42M.
factors.citation: Commerce Case Nos. A-557-831, A-549-843, A-555-101, A-552-842 (CSPV Cambodia/Malaysia/Thailand/Vietnam); 19 U.S.C. §1673; USITC Pub. 5570

factors.title: Section 301 Tariff Escalation on Chinese Modules and Inverters
factors.description: USTR's Section 301 List 3 action raised solar-grade polysilicon and PV cell/module tariffs (HTS 8541.40, 3818.00) to 50% effective 2024; a further escalation or new action targeting inverters (HTS 8504.40, Sungrow 60% share) could add $30–60M to procurement costs on top of existing tariff exposure on Jinko's Chinese-origin content.
factors.citation: USTR Section 301 Action (85 FR 67025); HTS 8541.40.6020, 8504.40.9550, 3818.00.0000; Presidential Proclamation May 2024 (tariff modifications)

factors.title: Solar Tracker and Steel Component Tariff Exposure
factors.description: Section 232 steel/aluminum tariffs and potential Section 201 safeguard modifications affect single-axis tracker systems (HTS 8479.89, 7308.90); a tracker supplier (likely steel-intensive imported components) price increase of 15–25% on an estimated $60M tracker budget translates to $9–15M in additional capex, compressing IRR by ~30–50 bps.
factors.citation: Presidential Proclamation 9705 (Section 232 steel); HTS 7308.90.9590, 8479.89.9499; USTR Section 201 Solar Safeguard (86 FR 12620)

factors.title: UFLPA Enforcement — Jinko Xinjiang Polysilicon Detention
factors.description: CBP UFLPA Entity List enforcement targets Xinjiang-origin polysilicon flowing through Jinko Solar's supply chain (HTS 3818.00, 8541.40); with Jinko comprising 55% of module supply (~330 MW), a port detention event pending supply-chain documentation rebuttal could halt module delivery for 3–9 months, threatening COD and triggering $45–75M in delay costs and PPA penalties.
factors.citation: Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act, Pub. L. 117-78; CBP UFLPA Entity List (FLETF); 19 U.S.C. §1307; CBP Withhold Release Order (WRO) precedents

factors.title: China Export Controls on Solar-Grade Polysilicon
factors.description: Beijing's Commerce Ministry has signaled potential export controls on polysilicon and solar manufacturing technology under China's Export Control Law (2020) in retaliation for US tariff and UFLPA actions; a restriction or licensing regime on Chinese polysilicon exports would constrict global supply, pushing spot module prices up 20–35% and adding $18–30M to the uncontracted module procurement budget.
factors.citation: China Export Control Law (Oct. 2020); MOFCOM Announcement No. 38 (2023, gallium/germanium precedent); Chinese Ministry of Commerce dual-use controls

factors.title: Sungrow Inverter Supply Disruption or Sanctions Risk
factors.description: Sungrow (60% of inverter supply) is a Chinese-headquartered manufacturer with US revenue exposure; escalating US–China technology decoupling, potential BIS Entity List designation, or secondary sanctions related to Xinjiang or military-civil fusion programs could restrict import of Sungrow inverters (HTS 8504.40), requiring costly re-specification to SMA or ABB alternatives with 6–12 month lead times.
factors.citation: Export Administration Regulations (EAR), 15 CFR §744; BIS Entity List (15 CFR Part 774, Supp. 4); EO 13959 (Chinese Military-Industrial Complex); HTS 8504.40.9550

factors.title: Interest Rate Elevated — Tax Equity and Debt Cost Compression
factors.description: With Fed Funds rate sustained above 4.5% through H1 2025 and long-end Treasury yields (10Y UST) at 4.3–4.7%, project finance debt pricing at SOFR+175–225 bps compresses levered equity IRR by 80–150 bps versus the 10% underwrite; a 100 bps increase in the all-in cost of the ~$420M senior debt tranche reduces NPV by approximately $18–25M through higher DSCR constraints and reduced leverage capacity.
factors.citation: FOMC Statement (Jan. 2025); Bloomberg SOFR forward curve; S&P Global infrastructure loan pricing survey Q1 2025

factors.title: BOEM COP Approval Delay or Denial
factors.description: The Construction and Operations Plan for OCS-A 0501 remains subject to BOEM review; the current administration has paused new offshore-wind leasing and signaled broader permitting reviews that could delay or rescind COP approval, pushing COD beyond Q4 2028 and triggering OREC contract penalties or renegotiation clauses.
factors.citation: EO 14154 (Jan 20, 2025) — 'Unleashing American Energy'; BOEM COP review docket for OCS-A 0501; 30 CFR Part 585

factors.title: IRC §45Y / §48E Credit Repeal or Phase-Down
factors.description: Congressional reconciliation efforts under the 119th Congress include proposals to repeal or accelerate the phase-down of the §45Y PTC and §48E ITC for offshore wind; loss of the full PTC (est. ~$28/MWh at 2025 rates) would reduce project NPV by collapsing the LCOE stack underpinning OREC pricing.
factors.citation: IRC §45Y, §48E (Inflation Reduction Act, P.L. 117-169); House Budget Reconciliation draft, 119th Cong. (2025)

factors.title: Treasury §45Y Domestic-Content Adder Denial
factors.description: Treasury's forthcoming final rules on the §45Y domestic-content adder (10 pp. bonus ITC/PTC) impose manufactured-product and steel/iron requirements; monopiles sourced from POSCO/South Korea and EEW SPC/Vietnam are unlikely to qualify, eliminating the bonus credit worth roughly $0.3B in NPV uplift that the project's OREC pricing model assumes.
factors.citation: IRC §45Y(g)(11); IRS Notice 2023-29, Notice 2024-41; Proposed Reg. REG-110412-23

factors.title: Section 232 Tariff Escalation on Korean Steel Monopiles
factors.description: POSCO-supplied monopile steel plate (HTS 7208.51, 7208.52) is currently subject to a 25% Section 232 tariff with a South Korea quota arrangement; any presidential proclamation terminating or reducing the quota exemption, or imposing derivative-product duties on fabricated monopiles, would increase landed steel cost by an estimated $45–60M on the POSCO tranche alone.
factors.citation: Proclamation 9705 (Mar 8, 2018); Proclamation 9740 (Apr 30, 2018) — Korean quota arrangement; HTS 7208.51.0060, 7208.52.0000; 19 USC §1862

factors.title: AD/CVD or Section 301 Duties on Vietnam Monopile Fabrication
factors.description: EEW SPC's Vietnam-fabricated monopiles (HTS 7308.20) face exposure to anti-dumping / countervailing-duty petitions from US steel and fabrication interests, as well as potential Section 301 List 4B extension to Vietnamese structural steel products; a 25–50% duty on the Vietnam tranche would add $60–100M to procurement cost.
factors.citation: HTS 7308.20.0000; USTR Section 301 Four-List Review (2024); potential AD/CVD petition under 19 USC §1673

factors.title: Section 201 Safeguard Extension on Wind Tower Components
factors.description: The existing Section 201 safeguard on large wind towers and tower sections (HTS 7308.20) expires on a rolling schedule; a USITC four-year extension review could broaden scope to cover offshore monopole substructures, adding incremental duties of 15–20% on imported fabricated steel substructures and increasing EPC cost by an estimated $50–70M.
factors.citation: Presidential Proclamation 9693 (Jan 23, 2018); 19 USC §2253; USITC Inv. No. TA-201-075; HTS 7308.20.0000

factors.title: Siemens Gamesa Supply-Chain Concentration and Export Control Risk
factors.description: 100% turbine supply from a single Danish OEM creates single-source concentration risk; escalating US–EU trade frictions or potential export-control harmonization measures on dual-use electrical machinery (ECCN 3A999 / EAR99 permanent magnet drivetrains with Chinese rare-earth inputs) could trigger licensing delays or supply disruptions affecting turbine delivery schedules critical to the Q4 2028 COD.
factors.citation: EAR Part 744; ECCN 3A999; EU Dual-Use Regulation 2021/821; potential Foreign Direct Product Rule application

factors.title: UFLPA Enforcement on Vietnamese Steel Supply Chain
factors.description: CBP enforcement of the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act creates rebuttable-presumption detention risk for Vietnamese-origin monopile fabrications if upstream steel inputs are traced to Xinjiang-linked Chinese mills; detention at port could delay monopile delivery by 6–18 months, causing liquidated damages under the OREC contract and forcing costly re-procurement.
factors.citation: P.L. 117-78 (UFLPA); CBP UFLPA Entity List; 19 USC §1307; FLETF Strategic Plan 2022

factors.title: Long-Term Interest Rate Spike Eroding Equity IRR
factors.description: The project's 8.5% target equity IRR is modeled on a ~5.0% long-term Treasury base; a 75–100 bps parallel shift in the 10-year and 30-year curve (driven by persistent fiscal deficits or stagflation) would increase project WACC, compress levered equity returns to sub-7%, and potentially trigger OREC re-opener clauses or require equity re-pricing that dilutes sponsor returns.
factors.citation: Internal IRR sensitivity model; Federal Reserve SEP (Mar 2025); US 10-yr Treasury yield dynamics

factors.title: Construction Cost Inflation and USD/EUR FX Exposure
factors.description: Approximately 60% of capex is denominated in EUR (Siemens Gamesa turbines, Prysmian cable) and KRW (POSCO steel); a 10% USD depreciation against EUR and KRW relative to the base-case FX assumptions embedded in the EPC contract would increase total capex by ~$170–200M, compressing equity IRR by roughly 60–80 bps absent contractual FX hedges.
factors.citation: Internal FX model; EPC contract FX exposure schedule; EUR/USD and USD/KRW forward curves (Q1 2025)

factors.title: IRC §48E Standalone Storage ITC Recapture Risk
factors.description: Treasury and IRS have not finalized prevailing-wage and apprenticeship (PWA) guidance for §48E standalone storage projects with COD in 2026; failure to satisfy PWA requirements reduces the ITC rate from 30% to 6%, eliminating approximately $72M in expected tax credit value. Proposed regulations published in August 2023 remain partially finalized, creating compliance uncertainty for a Q1 2026 COD.

factors.title: FEOC Restriction Disqualifies CATL/BYD Cells from §48E
factors.description: The Inflation Reduction Act's Foreign Entity of Concern (FEOC) provisions, as interpreted under proposed Treasury guidance, risk disqualifying battery systems containing CATL or BYD cells from the full §48E ITC beginning in 2025; with 80% of cell supply from Chinese-domiciled FEOC-designated entities, up to $96M of ITC basis could be at risk. Final FEOC rules for stationary storage are expected mid-2025 and could retroactively affect procurement already under contract.
factors.citation: IRC §48E(d)(4); IRS Notice 2024-05; IRS REG-118492-23

factors.title: IRC §45X Advanced Manufacturing PTC Guidance Delay
factors.description: Final Treasury rules for §45X electrode active materials and battery cell PTCs have not fully clarified whether LFP cells assembled outside the US but using domestically processed materials qualify; uncertainty threatens ~$15M in anticipated §45X passthrough credits embedded in LG Energy Solution supply pricing. Any narrowing of eligible components in final rulemaking would increase effective cell costs.
factors.citation: IRC §45X; IRS REG-107423-23; Treasury Final Rule (Dec 2024)

factors.title: FERC Order 2222 CAISO Implementation Stall
factors.description: CAISO's compliance filing for FERC Order 2222 DER aggregation remains contested; delays in final CAISO tariff implementation could prevent the project from stacking ancillary-service and capacity revenues beyond the SCE RA contract, directly reducing projected merchant revenue that underpins the 12% equity IRR. A 12-month implementation delay could reduce NPV by depressing post-COD cash flows during the critical 2026–2027 ramp period.
factors.citation: FERC Order No. 2222 (Sept 2020); CAISO Compliance Filing ER21-377

factors.title: Section 301 Tariff Escalation on LFP Cells (HTS 8507.60)
factors.description: The Biden administration raised Section 301 tariffs on Chinese lithium-ion batteries (HTS 8507.60.00) from 7.5% to 25% effective September 2024; the Trump administration is reviewing additional escalation to 35–50% as part of a broader China trade action, which would increase cell procurement costs for CATL and BYD supply by $24–48M above current budgets. A tariff hike announced before the project's final cell shipments in Q3–Q4 2025 would directly erode equity returns.
factors.citation: USTR Section 301 Four-Year Review; HTS 8507.60.00; FR Vol. 89 No. 88 (May 2024)

factors.title: AD/CVD Investigation on Chinese BESS Components
factors.description: A domestic-industry petition for antidumping and countervailing duties on Chinese battery energy storage system components, including power conversion systems and battery modules, is anticipated following the June 2024 AD/CVD petition on solar cells; if filed and preliminary duties imposed, Sungrow PCS equipment (50% of inverter supply, HTS 8504.40) could face 50–200% preliminary duties before COD. This would require emergency re-sourcing or absorb $20–40M in additional costs.
factors.citation: 19 U.S.C. §1673; HTS 8504.40.95; precedent: CVD Case C-570-979

factors.title: UFLPA Enforcement Action on LFP Cell Shipments
factors.description: CBP has expanded UFLPA Entity List enforcement to battery supply chains linked to Xinjiang-sourced lithium carbonate and graphite; CATL and BYD supply chains have documented exposure to Xinjiang materials, and a CBP detention order on inbound cell shipments could halt procurement for 60–120 days, jeopardizing Q1 2026 COD and triggering SCE RA contract penalties. Project faces $12–20M in delay costs and potential $8M liquidated damages under the offtake agreement.
factors.citation: Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (P.L. 117-78); CBP UFLPA Entity List (updated 2024); 19 U.S.C. §1307

factors.title: China Export Controls on Battery-Grade Graphite/Lithium
factors.description: China imposed export licensing requirements on natural graphite and related materials in October 2023 and has signaled further controls on lithium processing chemicals in retaliation for US chip export restrictions; tightening of these controls in 2025 would constrain CATL and BYD production capacity, causing cell delivery delays of 3–6 months and a 10–20% spot-price premium on contracted volumes. With 80% of cells from Chinese suppliers, supply disruption risk is concentrated.
factors.citation: China MOFCOM Announcement No. 33 (Oct 2023); China Export Control Law (2020 Art. 9); EO 13959 analogs

factors.title: CATL US Treasury SDN / Sanctions Designation Risk
factors.description: Bipartisan legislation (BIOSECURE Act analogs and proposed CATL-specific bills) and DoD Section 1260H 'Chinese Military Company' list inclusion of CATL create a risk of Treasury OFAC secondary-sanctions exposure or federal contract counterparty restrictions that could force contract termination with the company's largest cell supplier mid-procurement. Replacement sourcing at comparable cost and timeline is not feasible within the COD schedule.
factors.citation: DoD §1260H List (FY2024 NDAA); S.3834 Protecting America's Battery Supply Chain Act; 50 U.S.C. §1701

factors.title: Interest Rate Sensitivity on Construction Financing Cost
factors.description: The project's $400M capex is partially financed through a tax-equity bridge and construction loan priced at SOFR + 175 bps; if the Fed maintains higher-for-longer policy and SOFR remains above 4.5% through mid-2025, financing costs increase by approximately $6–9M versus the underwriting base case of a 75 bps rate cut cycle, compressing equity IRR below the 12% target. A 100 bps adverse rate move reduces project NPV by an estimated $12M.
factors.citation: Federal Reserve FOMC projections (Dec 2024 SEP); SOFR term rate; IRC §45Q tax-equity market benchmarks

factors.title: §45V Three-Pillars Final Rule Stringency
factors.description: Treasury's January 2025 final rule on §45V mandates hourly matching, incrementality, and deliverability by 2028; if the hourly-matching or incrementality requirements survive legal challenge and remain unamended, the project's H₂ lifecycle emissions intensity may exceed the 0.45 kg CO₂e/kg H₂ threshold required to claim the full $3/kg credit, collapsing project economics.
factors.citation: IRC §45V; Treasury Final Rule TD 10024 (Jan 3, 2025); 26 CFR §1.45V-4

factors.title: §45V Regulatory Rollback or Credit Repeal Risk
factors.description: Congressional reconciliation efforts in 2025 include proposals to repeal or curtail IRA clean-energy credits including §45V; a successful reconciliation bill eliminating or phasing out the hydrogen production credit before the project's COD would remove up to $3/kg of revenue support underpinning the equity return.
factors.citation: IRC §45V; House Budget Reconciliation Discussion Draft (Feb 2025); IRA §13204

factors.title: DOE H2Hubs Milestone Clawback or Funding Freeze
factors.description: DOGE-driven budget reviews and executive directives freezing IRA/IIJA grant disbursements could delay or cancel DOE H2Hubs cooperative agreement tranches; a funding freeze or milestone-default clawback on the project's Hub allocation would require replacement equity or debt at materially higher cost.
factors.citation: IIJA §40314 (H2Hubs, 42 U.S.C. §16161a); DOE Cooperative Agreement DE-EE0010679; EO 14154 (Jan 20, 2025)

factors.title: EPA Subpart W/RR Hydrogen Reporting Finalization
factors.description: EPA's finalization of Subpart RR (hydrogen production GHG reporting under 40 CFR Part 98) will determine the emissions accounting methodology used for §45V credit verification; a more conservative lifecycle methodology than modeled could push the project's carbon intensity above the top credit tier.
factors.citation: EPA 40 CFR Part 98 Subpart W/RR; EPA Proposed Rule 88 FR 65460 (Sep 2023); IRC §45V(c)(1)(B)

factors.title: Section 301 / AD-CVD Tariffs on Solar Module Inputs
factors.description: The co-located 200 MW+ solar array depends on PV modules; expanded Section 301 tariffs or anti-dumping/countervailing duty orders on solar cells and modules from Southeast Asian transshipment countries (Cambodia, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam) under existing CBP circumvention findings could increase solar capex by 15–25%, compressing the project's renewable energy cost stack.
factors.citation: Section 301, 19 U.S.C. §2411; USTR 4-List HTS 8541.40; AD/CVD Case A-570-979; CAATSA Circumvention Inquiry CBP 2022-02

factors.title: Tariffs on Imported Electrolyzer Components
factors.description: Nel Hydrogen (Norway) alkaline electrolyzers (20% share, ~$48M capex) and key stack components sourced from Europe or Asia face potential Section 232 tariff expansion or new reciprocal tariff schedules; a 25% tariff on HTS 8421.39 / 8501.40 industrial electrolytic equipment would directly increase equipment procurement cost.
factors.citation: Section 232, 19 U.S.C. §1862; HTS 8421.39.80, 8501.40.20; EO 14257 (Apr 2, 2025 'Liberation Day' tariffs); USTR Reciprocal Tariff Framework

factors.title: UFLPA Enforcement on PEM Stack Materials
factors.description: Proton exchange membranes, iridium-coated titanium components, and platinum-group catalysts used in Plug Power and Cummins/Accelera PEM stacks have upstream supply chains traceable to Xinjiang or sanctioned entities; a CBP UFLPA withhold order on shipments would halt electrolyzer deliveries and delay COD.
factors.citation: UFLPA, P.L. 117-78; CBP Operational Guidance (Jun 2022); HTS 3926.90, 8421.39; UFLPA Entity List

factors.title: Critical Mineral Supply Concentration — Iridium/Platinum
factors.description: PEM electrolyzers require iridium (>80% of global supply from South Africa and Zimbabwe) and platinum as catalysts; geopolitical instability in southern Africa, export restrictions, or a supply squeeze driven by growing global electrolyzer deployment could spike iridium spot prices (currently ~$5,000/troy oz) and inflate replacement/warranty costs for a 20-year asset.
factors.citation: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 (Iridium, Platinum); EO 13817 (Critical Minerals); DOE Critical Materials Assessment 2023

factors.title: Norway Export Controls on Electrolyzer Technology
factors.description: Nel Hydrogen's alkaline systems are manufactured in Norway; escalating NATO-Russia tensions or Norwegian government review of dual-use technology exports could subject advanced electrolyzer stack shipments to export-license delays under Norwegian Strategic Goods regulations, disrupting the construction schedule and triggering delay liquidated damages.
factors.citation: Norwegian Export Control Act (Lov om eksportkontroll); EU Dual-Use Regulation 2021/821; EAR 15 CFR §734 (US re-export considerations for US-origin content)

factors.title: SOFR / Treasury Rate Sensitivity on Project Debt
factors.description: The project's estimated $720M+ of senior debt (assumed ~60% leverage) is exposed to long-end rate levels at financial close (~2027); a sustained 100 bps increase in 10-year Treasury yields relative to current model assumptions would widen the all-in cost of debt and reduce levered equity IRR by approximately 150–200 bps, potentially breaching the 11% target hurdle.
factors.citation: FOMC SEP (Mar 2025); CME FedWatch; Bloomberg SOFR forward curve

factors.title: NEVI Program Funding Rescission or Freeze
factors.description: The Trump administration paused NEVI formula-fund disbursements in January 2025 pending program review; a prolonged freeze or rescission of unobligated state allocations would eliminate the primary funding source for roughly 60–70% of planned station deployments across the 8-state corridor, triggering revenue shortfalls and potential contract terminations.
factors.citation: 23 USC 175; FHWA Notice of Review Jan 2025; Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA) §11401

factors.title: IRC §30C Tax Credit Repeal or Phase-Down
factors.description: Reconciliation legislation advancing in the 119th Congress targets elimination or material reduction of the Alternative Fuel Vehicle Refueling Property Credit (§30C), which provides up to 30% / $100K per station credit; loss of this credit would reduce after-tax equity returns by approximately 150–200 bps and impair project-level cash flows on commercially-funded stations not covered by NEVI.
factors.citation: IRC §30C; House Ways & Means Committee reconciliation markup, April 2025

factors.title: FHWA BABA Waiver Denial or Tightening
factors.description: FHWA's Buy America Build America rules require domestically manufactured charging equipment; ABB Terra (Swiss) and Wallbox/Hypercharger (Spanish) together represent 65% of the supply mix and currently rely on general or product-specific waivers — tightened waiver standards or outright denial would force costly domestic-content substitution or disqualify stations from NEVI reimbursement.
factors.citation: 41 USC 8301 et seq.; 23 CFR 635.410; FHWA Buy America EV Charger Guidance, FY2024; Build America Buy America Act §70901-70952 IIJA

factors.title: FHWA Minimum Standards Rule Revision
factors.description: FHWA's 23 CFR Part 680 sets technical minimums (uptime, connector type, payment, accessibility) for NEVI-funded stations; a regulatory rollback removing mandatory uptime requirements (currently 97%) or open-payment mandates could undermine state offtake contract terms and trigger renegotiation penalties with site hosts, while a tightening of standards could impose retrofit capex.
factors.citation: 23 CFR Part 680; FHWA Final Rule 88 FR 12724 (Feb 2023); potential NPRM under EO 14192 deregulatory review

factors.title: Section 301 / New Tariffs on Swiss and EU Charger Components
factors.description: ABB Terra units (Switzerland, 40% supply share) and Wallbox/Hypercharger units (Spain/EU, 25% share) are subject to potential escalation of Section 301 or new reciprocal tariffs on electrical apparatus and EV charging equipment (HTS 8504.40, 8544.42); the April 2025 'reciprocal tariff' framework included a 20% baseline EU rate before the 90-day pause, and reinstatement would add $18–24M in equipment procurement costs.
factors.citation: HTS 8504.40.95; HTS 8544.42.90; EO 14257 (Reciprocal Tariffs, Apr 2025); USTR Section 301 List modifications

factors.title: AD/CVD or Section 201 Action on Chinese Power Electronics
factors.description: Key subcomponents in ABB, Wallbox, and ChargePoint units — including IGBT modules, rectifiers, and power conversion assemblies — are manufactured in or sourced from China; expansion of existing AD/CVD orders or a new Section 201 safeguard on power electronics (HTS 8501.40, 8504.40) could increase bill-of-materials costs by 15–25% and extend lead times by 3–6 months, compressing margins on the rolling 2025–2027 COD schedule.
factors.citation: HTS 8501.40.60; HTS 8504.40.95; AD/CVD Case A-570 series (inverters/power electronics); potential USITC Section 201 petition

factors.title: Supply Concentration in China-Dependent Power Semiconductors
factors.description: Gallium nitride and silicon carbide semiconductors used in high-power DC-DC conversion stages are predominantly manufactured or processed in China; China's December 2023 export controls on gallium and germanium and potential expansion to SiC substrates could cause 6–12 month supply disruptions, force spot-market procurement at 2–3× contract prices, and jeopardize COD dates for the 2025 tranche of stations.
factors.citation: China MOFCOM Gallium/Germanium Export Control Order (Aug 2023, effective Dec 2023); potential SiC controls under China Export Control Law Art. 9

factors.title: UFLPA Enforcement on Charger Sub-Assembly Supply Chain
factors.description: U.S. Customs and Border Protection has expanded UFLPA Entity List enforcement to electronics and EV-related goods with Xinjiang-linked supply chains; ABB and Wallbox units with components sourced from flagged Chinese contract manufacturers could face CBP detention at port of entry, requiring costly supply-chain audits, country-of-origin re-documentation, or supplier replacement that delays equipment delivery and triggers NEVI milestone penalties.
factors.citation: Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (PL 117-78); CBP UFLPA Entity List (updated 2024–2025); 19 USC 1307

factors.title: Elevated Long-End Rates Compressing Equity IRR
factors.description: The project targets a 13.0% equity IRR underwritten at a ~6.5–7.0% construction/term debt rate; a sustained 50–75 bps increase in the 10-year Treasury (currently pricing above 4.4%) would raise all-in borrowing costs and compress levered IRR below the 12% LP hurdle, potentially triggering equity re-pricing requirements or forcing additional sponsor equity contributions to maintain DSCR covenants across the rolling multi-state portfolio.
factors.citation: Federal Reserve FOMC projections (Mar 2025 SEP); 10-yr UST benchmark; project financing term sheet assumptions

factors.title: EV Adoption Slowdown Reducing Utilization Revenue
factors.description: Project revenue underwriting assumes 18–22% utilization rates by 2027 based on EV fleet penetration forecasts; a sustained macroeconomic slowdown, consumer spending contraction, or slower-than-projected EV adoption (exacerbated by potential rollback of §45W commercial clean vehicle credits) could compress utilization to 10–13%, reducing annual revenue by $8–12M and pushing IRR below target thresholds for commercially-funded stations in lower-traffic corridor segments.
factors.citation: IRC §45W; BloombergNEF EV Outlook 2025; FHWA traffic volume data; EIA Annual Energy Outlook 2025
